segments.narration: An angry orange orb chased two police cruisers at midnight. In January 1975, patrolmen in Mansfield, Massachusetts watched a blazing light lock onto their vehicles.
The silent object hovered just feet above the roof, glowing with enough heat to warp the paint. When the cruiser accelerated to ninety miles an hour, the light matched every turn.
Radio dispatchers listened in sheer panic as officers screamed for backup from a phantom pursuer. Civil defense radar confirmed an unlisted target tracking them from the clouds.

Decades of speculation dissolved when atmospheric physicists solved the chase. The cruisers had driven directly beneath high-voltage power lines during a rare ice storm, generating localized ball lightning.
A floating bubble of supercharged air acted like a living shadow. Could glowing air really mimic an intelligent pursuer?
